mcqs.question: Which of the following statements best expresses Le Chatelier’s principle?

options.A: If a stress is applied to a system at equilibrium, the system shifts in a direction that counteracts the stress and establishes a new equilibrium.
options.B: A system at equilibrium will always shift towards the side that has more moles of gas when temperature is increased.
options.C: Adding a catalyst to a system at equilibrium changes the concentrations of reactants and products.
options.D: Le Chatelier’s principle applies only to changes in concentration, not to pressure or temperature.

mcqs.answer: If a stress is applied to a system at equilibrium, the system shifts in a direction that counteracts the stress and establishes a new equilibrium.
mcqs.explanation: Le Chatelier’s principle states that when a dynamic equilibrium is subjected to a change in concentration, pressure, or temperature, the system responds by shifting in the direction that tends to oppose that change, thereby establishing a new equilibrium. Options B, C and D are incorrect because they misstate the principle or limit its scope.

mcqs.question: When the concentration of a reactant in a reversible reaction at equilibrium is increased, the equilibrium will shift:

options.A: Towards the products to consume the added reactant.
options.B: Towards the reactants to produce more reactant.
options.C: It will not shift; the position remains unchanged.
options.D: It will shift in the direction that produces the greatest increase in total pressure.

mcqs.answer: Towards the products to consume the added reactant.
mcqs.explanation: Increasing the concentration of a reactant creates a stress. According to Le Chatelier’s principle, the system counteracts this by shifting toward the side that uses the added reactant, i.e., toward the products. Options B, C, and D do not follow the principle.

mcqs.question: For the gaseous equilibrium N₂(g) + 3 H₂(g) ⇌ 2 NH₃(g), what is the effect of increasing the total pressure on the position of equilibrium?

options.A: The equilibrium shifts toward the side with fewer gas molecules (right, forming NH₃).
options.B: The equilibrium shifts toward the side with more gas molecules (left, forming N₂ and H₂).
options.C: There is no shift; pressure changes do not affect equilibria involving gases.
options.D: The direction of shift depends on the temperature of the system.

mcqs.answer: The equilibrium shifts toward the side with fewer gas molecules (right, forming NH₃).
mcqs.explanation: Increasing pressure by reducing volume favors the side of the reaction that occupies fewer moles of gas. Here, the product side has 2 mol of gas versus 4 mol on the reactant side, so the equilibrium shifts right. Options B, C, and D are incorrect.

mcqs.question: Consider the exothermic reversible reaction: 2 SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2 SO₃(g) + heat. If the temperature of the system is increased, what will happen to the equilibrium position?

options.A: The equilibrium will shift to the left (toward reactants).
options.B: The equilibrium will shift to the right (toward products).
options.C: There will be no shift; temperature does not affect equilibrium position.
options.D: The equilibrium constant will increase, but the position will remain unchanged.

mcqs.answer: The equilibrium will shift to the left (toward reactants).
mcqs.explanation: Increasing temperature adds heat to the system. For an exothermic reaction, heat is a product; the system counteracts the added heat by shifting toward the reactants (the endothermic direction). Hence the equilibrium moves left. Options B, C, and D misinterpret the effect of temperature.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand effect of catalysts on equilibrium
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes the effect of adding a catalyst to a chemical system that is already at equilibrium?

options.A: The catalyst speeds up only the forward reaction, shifting the equilibrium toward products.
options.B: The catalyst speeds up only the reverse reaction, shifting the equilibrium toward reactants.
options.C: The catalyst speeds up both forward and reverse reactions equally, so the equilibrium position remains unchanged.
options.D: The catalyst changes the equilibrium constant, thereby altering the composition at equilibrium.

mcqs.answer: The catalyst speeds up both forward and reverse reactions equally, so the equilibrium position remains unchanged.
mcqs.explanation: A catalyst lowers the activation energy for both forward and reverse reactions by the same amount, increasing the rate at which equilibrium is reached but not changing the equilibrium constant or the position. Options A, B, and D incorrectly claim a shift or change in K.

mcqs.question: A sealed container holds the gaseous equilibrium: 2 NO₂(g) ⇌ N₂O₄(g). The volume of the container is suddenly decreased, raising the total pressure. According to Le Chatelier’s principle, what will happen to the system?

options.A: The equilibrium will shift toward N₂O₄(g) because it has fewer gas molecules.
options.B: The equilibrium will shift toward 2 NO₂(g) because it has more gas molecules.
options.C: There will be no shift; pressure changes do not affect equilibria involving only gases.
options.D: The system will shift in the direction that absorbs heat, regardless of pressure.

mcqs.answer: The equilibrium will shift toward N₂O₄(g) because it has fewer gas molecules.
mcqs.explanation: Reducing volume increases pressure. Le Chatelier’s principle predicts a shift toward the side with fewer moles of gas to relieve the pressure increase. Here, N₂O₄(g) occupies one mole versus two moles of NO₂(g), so the equilibrium moves right. Options B, C, and D are inconsistent with the principle.

mcqs.question: A student claims that adding more product to a reaction at equilibrium will always increase the rate of the forward reaction. Which of the following statements correctly addresses this misconception?

options.A: Adding product increases its concentration, causing the reverse reaction to speed up and the equilibrium to shift toward reactants.
options.B: Adding product has no effect on either forward or reverse reaction rates.
options.C: Adding product speeds up the forward reaction because the system tries to use the extra product.
options.D: The forward reaction rate is independent of product concentration, so the equilibrium does not shift.

mcqs.answer: Adding product increases its concentration, causing the reverse reaction to speed up and the equilibrium to shift toward reactants.
mcqs.explanation: Increasing the concentration of a product creates a stress that the system counteracts by favoring the reverse reaction, shifting equilibrium toward reactants. This corrects the misconception that the forward reaction speeds up. Options B, C, and D misrepresent the effect of product concentration on reaction rates and equilibrium.

mcqs.question: Why does increasing the pressure of a gaseous equilibrium favor the side with fewer gas molecules?

options.A: Because the side with fewer molecules occupies a smaller volume, reducing the system’s overall pressure.
options.B: Because the kinetic energy of molecules decreases with pressure, making the reaction slower on the side with more molecules.
options.C: Because the concentration of each gas becomes equal, nullifying the effect of pressure.
options.D: Because temperature automatically rises with pressure, shifting the equilibrium toward the endothermic direction.

mcqs.answer: Because the side with fewer molecules occupies a smaller volume, reducing the system’s overall pressure.
mcqs.explanation: Increasing pressure (by decreasing volume) creates a stress that the system relieves by shifting toward the side that occupies less volume, i.e., the side with fewer gas molecules. This reduces the total pressure. Options B, C, and D give incorrect reasons unrelated to Le Chatelier’s principle.
